thesis: Applied Optoelectronics is a levered 800G catch-up story: Q1 2026 revenue $151.1M (+51% y/y) with first volume 800G shipments to a large hyperscaler, management claiming demand exceeds capacity through mid-2027, and a planned capacity ramp from 100K to 650K+ units/month by year-end 2026. But the company is still lossmaking (non-GAAP EPS -$0.07 in Q1, Q2 guided to roughly breakeven), gross margin is only 29-30% versus 45%+ at scale leaders, and the ~$7-10B market cap already prices the capacity ramp succeeding. History warns: AAOI has lost hyperscaler sockets abruptly before.
catalysts: 800G capacity ramp: 100K units/month (end Q1 2026) to 650K+ by year-end 2026
Q2 2026 results (August 2026): guidance $180-198M revenue, non-GAAP EPS -0.03 to +0.03 - the breakeven crossover quarter
Management expects 800G demand to exceed production capacity through mid-2027
CATV segment ($66.8M in Q1) providing a second leg unrelated to AI capex
risk_factors: Customer concentration: revenue historically dominated by two hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon lineage); a single dual-sourcing decision has cratered this company before
Profitability still fragile: GAAP net loss $14.3M in Q1 2026, non-GAAP loss, and Q1 missed both EPS and revenue expectations
Gross margin 29-30% - structurally below optics peers; little room for pricing pressure when supply normalizes
Massive capacity expansion (6.5x in a year) into a cyclical demand peak is the classic optics-cycle mistake
Beta 2.12; -6.33% past week as the AI-optics complex leaked; conflicting quotes ($121-162) suggest a fast-moving, volatile tape

q1_2026_revenue.note: +51% y/y; datacenter 81.4M, CATV 66.8M; first volume 800G shipments

q1_2026_net_loss_gaap.note: GAAP EPS -0.19; non-GAAP EPS -0.07 vs -0.05 expected

market_cap.note: conflicts with quoted price 121.26 (implies ~7.3B on ~60M shares); both figures retained, ~60M share count used for per-share math
